title: LIPITOR (atorvastatin calcium) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
authors: US Food and Drug Administration (labelling submitted by Viatris Specialty LLC)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration approved prescribing information, via DailyMed; version 8, effective 15 April 2024; sections 4 to 8 and 14
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: Contraindications: acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis; hypersensitivity, with anaphylaxis, angioneurotic oedema, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis reported. Warnings: atorvastatin may cause myopathy and rhabdomyolysis; acute kidney injury secondary to myoglobinuria and rare fatalities have occurred; risk factors are age 65 years or older, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, renal impairment, interacting drugs (CYP3A4, OATP1B1/1B3, P-gp and BCRP inhibitors, gemfibrozil, other fibrates, niacin 1 g/day or more, colchicine) and higher dose; muscle symptoms and creatine kinase rises may resolve on discontinuation. Rare immune-mediated necrotising myopathy with anti-HMG-CoA reductase antibodies, weakness and raised creatine kinase that persist after discontinuation, recurrence with the same or a different statin, and need for immunosuppressive treatment. Persistent transaminase rises above 3 times the upper limit of normal in 0.7% of patients in trials (0.2%, 0.2%, 0.6% and 2.3% on 10, 20, 40 and 80 mg); rare postmarketing fatal and non-fatal hepatic failure. Increases in HbA1c and fasting glucose. SPARCL post hoc analysis, 4731 patients with stroke or transient ischaemic attack in the previous 6 months, median 4.9 years: haemorrhagic stroke 55 (2.3%) on atorvastatin 80 mg against 33 (1.4%) on placebo (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.09 to 2.59), non-fatal 38 against 16, fatal 17 against 18; with haemorrhagic stroke at entry 16% against 4%; ischaemic stroke 9.2% against 11.6%; diabetes reported as an adverse reaction in 6.1% against 3.8%. TNT, 10,001 patients with coronary heart disease after an 8-week open-label run-in on atorvastatin 10 mg, median 4.9 years, 80 mg against 10 mg: serious adverse reactions 1.8% against 1.4%, discontinuation for adverse reactions 9.9% against 8.1%, all-cause deaths 284 (5.7%) against 282 (5.6%), HR 1.01 (0.85 to 1.19), non-cardiovascular deaths 158 (3.2%) against 127 (2.5%), HR 1.25 (0.99 to 1.57). Postmarketing reports: pancreatitis, fatal and non-fatal hepatic failure, anaphylaxis, tendon rupture, rhabdomyolysis, myositis, peripheral neuropathy, depression, interstitial lung disease, angioneurotic oedema, bullous rashes including erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis; rare cognitive impairment (memory loss, amnesia, confusion) reported with all statins, generally non-serious and reversible on discontinuation, onset 1 day to years, median resolution 3 weeks; rare new-onset or exacerbated myasthenia gravis, including ocular, with recurrence on the same or a different statin. Pregnancy: may cause fetal harm based on the mechanism of action, which decreases synthesis of cholesterol and possibly other biologically active substances derived from cholesterol; breastfeeding not recommended. Plasma concentrations about 40% (Cmax) and 30% (AUC) higher in healthy people aged 65 or older.
